To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed an algorithm that can exceed practicing radiologists in the detection of pneumonia from chest X-ray images, and we extended our algorithm to detect 14 different chest diseases.
we develop a deep neural network, CheXNet that detects pneumonia at a level exceeding radiologist performance.
CheXNet can detect pneumonia from frontal-view X-ray chest images at a level exceeding radiologists, and that CheXNet is state of the art for all diseases in ChestX-Ray14.

two questions: (1) Can a deep learning algorithm detect pneumonia from frontal-view chest X-rays at least as accurately as practicing radiologists?

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

our algorithm is the first to detect pneumonia at a radiologist-level, the first to detect all 13 diseases at a radiologist level, the first to outperform radiologists on F1 metric, and the first to achieve state of the arts results on all 13 diseases.
CheXNet is the state of the art for pneumonia detection in chest x-rays and it is the first algorithm to exceed radiologists in detecting pneumonia.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an algorithm that can outperform human radiologists in detecting pneumonia from chest X-ray images.
our algorithm, CheXnet, is a deep learning algorithm that can detect 5 common diseases in chest X-ray images, and it can detect pneumonia with an accuracy that surpasses radiologists.
we developed a deep learning algorithm that exceeds radiologist-level performance on pneumonia detection.
The main takeaway from our work is that

deep learning can be used to detect diseases from chest X-rays with performance comparable to practicing radiologists, and that deep learning algorithms can be developed on large datasets of deidentified images.
deep learning can detect disease on chest X-rays at or above radiologist-level performance.
deep convolutional neural networks trained on a large dataset with weak supervision can perform at a level exceeding radiologists.
